The vinculum, surviving as plain text

A third written as a decimal is 0.3̅, and the bar over the three is not decoration, it is the notation. U+0305, the combining overline, is how that bar exists as a character rather than as something a layout draws. Mathematicians call it a vinculum: x̅ for a mean, a bar over the repeating block of a decimal, an overline for negation in logic. Put it after the character you want it above and it draws on top instead of underneath.

The reason anyone needs this is that most of the places maths gets discussed have no equation editor: a chat box, a spreadsheet cell, a support ticket, a homework reply. Typing the bar as a character is the only way for the meaning to survive the trip, and there is no font to apply. The arithmetic bites here as elsewhere, though. A bar over four digits costs eight characters, and a platform that strips combining marks will hand back a plain x.

Also searched as: bar over text, line above text, vinculum generator, repeating decimal bar.

Where Overline text works, and where it does not

WorksWorks anywhere plain text goes, and is the only way to strike through or underline in a field that will not take formatting. Watch outEach mark is its own character, so the length counts against a bio limit even though nothing extra is visible. A few platforms strip combining marks on save.

Overline questions

How do I write a repeating decimal?

Overline the digits that repeat and leave the rest alone. A third is a nought, a point, then a three carrying the bar. For something like a seventh, where six digits repeat before coming round again, run all six through so the bar spans the whole block and stops where the repetition does.

Is the overline the same as a macron?

They are different characters doing different jobs. A macron marks a long vowel and belongs to a single letter, which is why precomposed forms like ā exist. The overline is a vinculum, meant to span whatever it covers, so it is the one you want for a mean, a repeat bar or a negation.

Can I put a bar over a whole expression?

Only by overlining each character in it, one mark apiece. Adjacent bars are drawn to sit alongside one another, so a run of them reads as a single line above the span. It is also why the character count doubles across the entire expression, which tells against you in a field with a tight limit.
